raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniCPM5 supports XML CDATA in tool arguments, but the outer block scan still treats a literal `</function>` inside CDATA as the end of the call. This matters when a tool writes XML or searches for markup.

For example, a `note` string containing `<function name="inner">content</function>` inside `<![CDATA[...]]>` is truncated before the XML parser sees it. A required parameter makes the call disappear; an optional parameter can instead be emitted as an empty argument dictionary. Streaming can emit that incomplete call before the CDATA section closes.

## Modifications

- Scan each function block for its closing boundary while skipping XML CDATA and comments.
- Parse the original, unmodified XML slice so CDATA values are preserved.
- Hold incomplete CDATA sections until a later chunk supplies their terminator.
- Add three regression methods to the existing MiniCPM5 test file using `CustomTestCase`.

Related work: #42577 replaces the non-streaming boundary scan for performance. Its full diff was reviewed; it does not handle CDATA, so this is a different correctness fix, but both touch the same scanning area and may need integration/rebasing. #41962 addresses end-of-stream flushing and is not included here.

## Accuracy Tests

Real CPU execution with the repository parser, OpenAI protocol types, XML implementation, and `CustomTestCase` (no source harness or fake product modules):

- Original code plus regressions: **15 passed, 2 failed**.
- Patched test file: **17 passed**, including **120 subtests** (all 114 two-chunk splits of the CDATA payload and six normal-text/comment regression cases).
- Direct registered-file invocation also passes: `python test/registered/unit/function_call/test_minicpm5_detector.py`.

No model weights, inference service, GPU test, or full server suite was used. This changes parser interpretation, not model forward computation. The local environment is Python 3.12 with CPU SGLang dependencies. Existing import warnings and an `asyncio_mode` warning from the absent optional pytest-asyncio plugin are disclosed; the target tests are synchronous.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput claim or model benchmark. The boundary scan skips CDATA and comment tokens within each function block; XML parsing still consumes the original text. This is not the separate performance work in #42577.

## Checklist

- [x] Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed, including Rust formatting and clippy.
- [x] Added failing-before/passing-after regression tests in the existing registered file.
- [x] Followed the existing XML/CDATA contract and code style; no new public API or documentation change required.
- [x] Accuracy/speed validation scope and limitations are stated above.

Developed with AI assistance and local regression testing.

@@ -30,6 +30,28 @@
     r"<param\s+name=[\'\"]([^\'\"]+)[\'\"]>([\s\S]*?)</param>", re.DOTALL
 )
 _PARAM_MISSING_NAME_REGEX = re.compile(r"<param(?![^>]*\bname=)[^>]*>", re.DOTALL)
+_FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r"<!--.*?(?:-->|\Z)|<!\[CDATA\[.*?(?:\]\]>|\Z)|</function>", re.DOTALL
+)
+
+
+def _find_function_end(text: str, start: int = 0) -> int:
+    # CDATA and comments contain data, not function boundaries. An unfinished
+    # section holds the call until a later chunk supplies its terminator.
+    for match in _FUNCTION_BOUNDARY_REGEX.finditer(text, start):
+        if match.group(0) == "</function>":
+            return match.end()
+    return -1
+
+
+def _iter_function_blocks(text: str):
+    start = text.find("<function")
+    while start != -1:
+        end = _find_function_end(text, start)
+        if end == -1:
+            return
+        yield start, end
+        start = text.find("<function", end)

 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
 register_cpu_ci(1.0, "base-a-test-cpu")
 
@@ -275,6 +276,72 @@ def test_malformed_xml_with_unescaped_ampersand_falls_back_to_regex():
     assert json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters)["city"] == "A & B"
 
 
+class TestMiniCPM5CDATA(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_function_end_inside_cdata_is_argument_text(self):
+        """Writing XML containing </function> must not truncate a CDATA argument
+        or lose the tool call, including when that token spans stream chunks."""
+        value = '<function name="inner">content</function>'
+        text = (
+            '<function name="noop"><param name="note"><![CDATA['
+            + value
+            + "]]></param></function>"
+        )
+        tools = make_tools_no_required()
+        result = MiniCPM5Detector().detect_and_parse(text, tools)
+        self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters), {"note": value})
+        for split in range(len(text) + 1):
+            with self.subTest(split=split):
+                detector = MiniCPM5Detector()
+                calls = []
+                for chunk in (text[:split], text[split:]):
+                    calls.extend(detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools).calls)
+                self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
+                self.assertEqual(json.loads(calls[0].parameters), {"note": value})
+
+    def test_unfinished_cdata_never_emits_a_partial_call(self):
+        """A literal closing-function tag inside an unfinished CDATA region is
+        not permission to invoke a tool with incomplete arguments."""
+        tools = make_tools_no_required()
+        prefix = '<function name="noop"><param name="note"><![CDATA[text </function>'
+        detector = MiniCPM5Detector()
+        self.assertEqual(detector.parse_streaming_increment(prefix, tools).calls, [])
+        result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+            " tail]]></param></function>", tools
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters), {"note": "text </function> tail"}
+        )
+
+    def test_cdata_markers_in_prose_or_comments_do_not_hide_calls(self):
+        """Only CDATA inside a function frames its arguments; prose and XML
+        comments can describe its opener without swallowing a later call."""
+        call = '<function name="noop"><param name="note">ok</param></function>'
+        cases = [
+            ("Example <![CDATA[ marker.\n" + call, 1),
+            (call + " Example <![CDATA[ marker. " + call, 2),
+            (call.replace("<param", "<!-- <![CDATA[ -->" + "<param", 1), 1),
+        ]
+        for text, count in cases:
+            for streaming in (False, True):
+                with self.subTest(text=text, streaming=streaming):
+                    detector = MiniCPM5Detector()
+                    if streaming:
+                        calls = detector.parse_streaming_increment(
+                            text, make_tools_no_required()
+                        ).calls
+                    else:
+                        calls = detector.detect_and_parse(
+                            text, make_tools_no_required()
+                        ).calls
+                    self.assertEqual(len(calls), count)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        [json.loads(item.parameters) for item in calls],
+                        [{"note": "ok"}] * count,
+                    )
+
+
